title: Values and types: prefix words and no implicit conversions
summary: In Omega every operation is a prefix word with a fixed number of inputs, so add mul a a 4 needs no brackets. Drake made types strict: no implicit conversions (error 7), a bare number needs a place that types it (error 11), and a conversion that does not fit traps 5 instead of truncating. I'll show you each one with a real refusal and its fix.
goal: Write typed Omega values and recognise errors 7 and 11 and trap 5.
key_steps: Write operations as prefix words: add mul a a 4
Give new numbers a type: x = uint 5
Convert explicitly where types differ: add ulong x 1
Mask before narrowing: uchar and big 255
Read error 7 as mixed types and error 11 as an untyped number

example.code:
note values.om: prefix words, typed numbers, unsigned wrap, a checked conversion
fn main to int
a = uint 7
b = add mul a a 4
note b = (7 * 7) + 4, a uint because a is a uint
c = uchar 255
d = add c 1
note uchar arithmetic wraps modulo 256, so d is 0
if ne d 0
ret 1
end
big = uint 300
low = uchar and big 255
note mask first, then convert: the value fits, so the conversion does not trap
if ne low 44
ret 2
end
ret int b
end
example.output:
omc sha256 befb8199db8c4bca188a494dfaac2a6f0ee5c36fcea11188c75666c55fce8a1d
== 1. values: exit status is the computed value b = 53
compile values.om rc=0
run values rc=53
== 2. trap 5: a conversion whose value does not fit (exit 100 + 5)
compile narrow.om rc=0
run narrow rc=105
== 3. error 7: no implicit conversion between uint and long
compile mixed.om rc=7
omc: line 4: error 7
== 4. error 11: a bare number with no type
compile bare.om rc=11
omc: line 3: error 11
== 5. the fix: say every type; 8 + 5 = 13
compile fixed.om rc=0
run fixed rc=13
RESULT PASS

common_mistake: Expecting implicit widening or narrowing. add x long 1 with x a uint is error 7; x = 5 for a new name is error 11; uchar of 300 traps 5 (exit 105). Fix: write the conversion yourself (add ulong x 1), type the number (uint 5), and mask before narrowing (uchar and big 255).
evidence_note: Compiled and run on Linux AArch64 with omc befb8199...8a1d; statuses 53, 105, 7, 11 and 13 recorded and reproduced byte for byte. Float rules are described in OMEGESE 9.9 but not exercised here.
